deep.reconstruction:
This page is the scratch side of a page from note 7 to note 8; the paper is the back of a Cray job banner dated 25 Aug 1982. The setting, carried over from the previous and next pages, is a category C with weak equivalences W and cofibrations Cof. Grothendieck is building a category C~ whose morphisms x → y are classes [f0, i] of 'fantaisistes'. A fantaisiste factors f as α∘f0, with f0: x ↣ ȳ a cofibration and α: ȳ →~ y in W admitting a section i. He wants to prove C~ ≅ W^{-1}C. The step needed here: any two factorizations x ↣ y' →~ y and x ↣ y'' →~ y of the same map are both dominated by a third, so they lie in one connected component of the category of such factorizations.

The diagrams carry out the standard argument.
(1) Take the two factorizations x ↣ y' → y and x ↣ y'' → y.
(2) Form the coproduct map x ⊔ x ↣ y' ⊔ y'', which is a cofibration as a sum of cofibrations. Induce y' ⊔ y'' → y.
(3) Factor that map as y' ⊔ y'' ↣ • →~ y. Then x ↣ • ↣ y gives a third factorization, receiving maps from y' and y''.
(4) The lower square diagram ('i1, i2, cocart') checks that x∨x → y'∨y'' is a cofibration. It does so by two cocartesian squares: x --i2--> x∨x ↣ y'∨x, then y'' → x∨y'' ↣ y'∨y''. That is, (f0', id) and (id, f0'') are pushouts of cofibrations, and their composite is the sum.
(5) Precomposing with the fold map ∇: x∨x → x gives the comparison.

The next page states this explicitly ('X ∨ X → Ȳ' ⊔ Ȳ', ∇_X, cocart'). It also notes that the new weak equivalence α'' inherits a section from α or α'. This reduces fidelity of C~ → W^{-1}C to the independence (**) of the class [1_X, i] from the choice of section i.
errors: None mathematically. Step (3) needs y'⊔y'' → • to be followed by a weak equivalence •→y, i.e. the 2-out-of-3 property. The requirement that the new α'' admits a section is handled on the next page, not here.

ideas.what: Two cofibration–weak equivalence factorizations of one map are dominated by a third, via the coproduct of cofibrations and a refactorization. Coproduct cofibrations are verified by pushouts.
ideas.modern_name: Connectedness (contractibility) of the category of factorizations; Brown's factorization lemma / categories of cofibrant objects; calculus of fractions up to homotopy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (Homotopical Algebra 1967), K.S. Brown (1973), Dwyer–Kan (1980), later Cisinski
ideas.where_published: Related material in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and Les Dérivateurs, but this specific argument is not identified there

ideas.what: Description of hom-sets of W^{-1}C as π0 of a category of 'fantaisistes' (cofibration followed by a weak equivalence with a section)
ideas.modern_name: Hammock localization / homotopy function complexes computed by spans

missed.claim: Dating evidence: Grothendieck was working on localization of categories with cofibrations and weak equivalences (Brown-style) on Cray printout paper dated 25 Aug 1982. This is months before Pursuing Stacks (Feb 1983) and supports the archive's '[à partir de 1982]'.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Helps date the archive notes, and shows the homotopical-algebra preoccupations of Pursuing Stacks were already active in 1982.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a standard model-category / cofibration-category argument. The only notable point is the dating evidence the printout supplies.
transcription_corrections: The symbols '∨' / '⊔' both denote the coproduct; the diagram reads x --i2--> x∨x ↣ y'∨x and y'' → x∨y'' ↣ y'∨y''. Labels i1, i2 are the coproduct inclusions.
The top diagram shows two factorizations x ↣ y' and x ↣ y'' with arrows to a common target, not a single line 'x ↣ y' y''.'
The crossed-out text after 'x ⊔ x ↣ y' ⊔ y''' is an arrow to y (struck through).
The bullet diagram reads x ↣ • ↣ y, with arrows from y' and y'' into •.
